Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back, folks. Which side is your money on? The sun is shining, these are good conditions but chasing 332 is a tough task for England. Philip Salt and Dawid Malan are the openers out in the middle for England. Shaheen Afridi has got the first new ball in his hand and he will swing the ball into the breeze. Here he is, running into Salt...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then. 332 to chase. Can Pakistan win their first game of the tour? The pitch looks good but there are rough patches on the surface as well, which will aid turn and the likes of Shadab and Shakeel will enjoy. But if it does not turn, then we are in for a fabulous run chase. Stay tuned for England's reply.

In a rare off day, England struggled with the ball. They felt things were under control when Imam and Babar were batting but were completely taken aback by the shift of gears from the Pakistan skipper and the mammoth 3rd-wicket stand. The attack was launched in the 33rd over, at which stage, Pakistan were 159/2. You can see the carnage in the last few overs. Brydon Carse and Saqib Mahmood pulled things back in the end with Carse using the short ball to perfection. He ended up with 5 in his pocket while Mahmood did a decent job in his last two overs.

Babar was joined by Rizwan and the duo utilized the momentum created by the previous pair. 179 runs were scored in just 120 balls as England were taken to the cleaners. Babar was actually batting slowly but Rizwan's urgency got the partnership rollicking and eventually, rubbed onto Babar as well, who just switched on a different gear once he reached the 80s. The skipper played beautifully for his 158 and it was an innings to savor. It was this stand between Babar and Rizwan which took Pakistan post 300. They lost 7 wickets in the last 5 overs but one feels that they have enough on the board.

Saqib Mahmood did begin well though, getting Fakhar Zaman early but after that it was all Pakistan. Imam-ul-Haq and Babar Azam played themselves into form and added 92 for the second wicket. Imam could have actually been dismissed LBW in the very first over but Ben Stokes chose not to review an LBW call, which was confirmed as plumb by the Ball Tracker. But the fun didn't end there.

Needless to say, this is a commanding score put by Pakistan on the board. For the first time in the series, the English bowlers were put under pressure. And when the wickets did not come as frequently as they did in the first two ODIs, they buckled. Yes, England finished well, picking up some quick wickets in the end but the target will not be an easy one to chase.
TWO TO END THE INNINGS! Short ball on middle, Shakeel pulls it to deep square leg and picks up a couple before the fielder cuts it off. PAKISTAN END ON 331 FOR 9.
Slower short ball outside off, Shakeel is early into his pull and misses.
Haris Rauf is the last man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! 5-fer for Brydon Carse! Pakistan 9 down now with two more balls to go! Short on off, Afridi looks to pull but it goes off the top edge to mid on where James Vince takes the simplest of catches. This has been a good finish from England.
Commentary.Howout: c James Vince b Brydon Carse

Commentary.Commentary: Short ball around off, Shakeel looks to pull but it goes off the inner half to fine leg for a single.
Shaheen Afridi is the next man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! The Edgbaston crowd stands and applauds for what has been a magnificent knock from Babar Azam.  Full ball outside off, Azam looks to lift it over the off side but it takes the top edge and goes to point where Dawid Malan takes a comfortable catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Dawid Malan b Brydon Carse

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Excellent start to the final over for Pakistan! Shortish on middle, Azam pulls it to deep square leg for a boundary.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Another one bites the dust! Pakistan are losing wickets in search for a big finish! Full outside off, Shadab Khan looks to drive it to the off side but it goes off the outside edge to John Simpson who takes a comfortable catch. One more over to go. Saud Shakeel is the next man in.
Commentary.Howout: c John Simpson b Saqib Mahmood

Commentary.Commentary: Shadab Khan makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! TIMBER! Faheem Ashraf goes but he has done his job. Good length ball on off, Ashraf looks to swing it away but is early into the shot. He misses and the ball uproots the timber. Pakistan are losing some wickets towards the end.
WIDE! Loose from Mahmood! Very full down the leg side, Ashraf looks to swing it away but misses. Wide given.
Mid on drops back to the boundary now.
Short ball around middle, Ashraf looks to pull but misses.
FOUR! EDGED AND FOUR! 10 from balls for Faheem Ashraf! Short ball around middle, Ashraf looks to pull but it takes the top edge and it goes over the keeper for a boundary.
SIX! What a start to his innings, Faheem Ashraf! Short ball on middle, Ashraf pulls it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum.
Fullish ball outside off, Azam lifts it to deep cover for one.

NOT OUT! Azam is in! Terrific throw from Dawid Malan. Good length ball outside off, Azam cuts it to point and takes off for a single. Malan collects and has a shy at the bowler's end and hits. The third umpire is called for and the replays show that Azam has dragged his bat in.
An appeal for run out taken upstairs! Babar Azam looks short of his crease. No, no he has made it in but by just.
Slower ball on middle, Azam waits for it and then pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Faheem Ashraf comes out now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Carse gets his third wicket and there will be no fireworks from Hasan Ali in this game! Short ball around off, Hasan Ali clears his front leg and looks to pull but it takes the top edge and goes to mid-wicket where Zak Crawley settles under it and takes a comfortable catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Zak Crawley b Brydon Carse

Commentary.Commentary: EDGED AND FOUR! Hasan Ali is away with a boundary. Good length ball around off, Ali looks to smack it to the leg side but gets a top edge and it goes over the keeper for a boundary.
Hasan Ali has been promoted up the order. No surprises here as Hasan has shown before that he can hit the long ball.

OUT! CAUGHT! The tactics of bowling short works for Brydon Carse! The dangerous Maqsood goes cheaply. He can be a dangerous batsman at the death. Short ball on middle, Maqsood looks to pull but fails to get the required timing and the distance on it. It goes to deep mid-wicket where James Vince takes the catch.
Commentary.Howout: c James Vince b Brydon Carse

Commentary.Commentary: 150 up for Babar Azam! First one in ODIs and it has been a dominant innings from the Pakistan skipper. Good length ball outside off, Azam punches it to deep cover for one to reach his milestone.
FOUR! Spoils the over! Short ball on middle and leg, Maqsood swivels and then pulls it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary. 8 runs from it.
Short ball around off, Maqsood sways away from it.
WIDE! Down the leg side, Maqsood moves across and looks to flick but misses. Wided. 300 up for Pakistan.
Very full outside off, Azam digs it out to deep point. Moves to 149 with a single.
WIDE! Very full way outside the tramline outside off, Azam does not play at that. Wided.
Excellent running! Mahmood bowls a low full toss outside off, Azam drives it wide of long off. Azam calls for two and makes it before the throw reaches to the keeper's end.
Good start from Mahmood! He bowls it full and outside off, just inside the tramline. Azam lets it go to the keeper.
Saqib mahmood is into the attack now. Can he finish well for England?
EDGED AND FOUR! Perfect start from Sohaib Maqsood! Good length ball around off, Maqsood shuffles across and then opens the face of the bat and then guides it to third man for a boundary.
Sohaib Maqsood comes out at number 5.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Rizwan walks off and this ends a very big partnership. A wonderful one for Pakistan. Mohammad Rizwan departs after playing an excellent knock. He gave this innings real impetus. Shortish down the leg side, Rizwan looks to pull but seems to have gotten the gloves back to the keeper, John Simpson who takes it. England appeal but the umpire waits for a long while before he raises the finger. Rizwan does not bother reviewing as he walks straight back to the pavilion. The Ultra Edge rolls in and it shows that there was gloves on it.
Commentary.Howout: c John Simpson b Brydon Carse

Commentary.Commentary: PLAY AND A MISS! Shortish on the pads, Rizwan takes a few steps forward and then looks to pull but fails to get any bat on it.
Short on middle, Azam clears his front leg and then looks to pull but mistimes it to mid on for one.

SIX! This is some hitting we are seeing the last few overs. Brilliant from Azam. Carse was looking for the yorker again but misses his length. Ends up bowling it full on middle, Azam lifts it over long on for a maximum.
Carse bowls a low full toss on middle, Rizwan works it to mid on and crosses over for a run.
Brydon Carse comes back on. 7-0-34-0 are his figures so far.
FOUR! A short ball, outside off, Babar pull it through mid-wicket for another boundary. 12 from the over, 68 in the last 6!
Similar ball, dabbed towards point for one more.
Outside off, angling away, Rizwan guides it towards third man for a run.
FOUR! Fuller, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan pushes it uppishly, to the left of the bowler, wide of mid off, to his right, to the fence down the ground. Rizwan moves to 70 from 53 balls.
A short ball, outside off, Babar pulls it towards fine leg for a single.

TOP EDGE, LANDS SAFELY! No idea how has that not been taken. A short ball, outside off, Babar Azam backs away and looks to pull. But the change of pace does him in. The top edge is induced and the ball goes straight up in the air. Matt Parkinson is there at mid off while Ben Stokes is at mid on. But both are at the edge of the circle and neither can get to the ball as it lands just beside the stumps at the bowler's end!
Short, around off, Azam backs away and punches it through cover for one. 13 from the over, 56 in the last 5!
SIX! Floated up by Parkinson, around off, Babar comes down the track and swings this through the line over long on! Babar moves to 133 from 124 balls.
Outside off, this is pushed through point for a run.
FOUR! Full, down the leg side, Mohammad Rizwan sweeps it past Dawid Malan at short fine leg, to his right, to meet the fence. 150-RUN STAND IS UP, IN 106 BALLS!
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.

DROPPED! Oh nearly! Juicy full toss, outside off, Babar Azam comes down the track and slams it towards short mid-wicket. Actually, he mishits it. But still, the ball goes powerfully to Brydon Carse over there, who cannot hang on.

Short, outside off, Rizwan punches it through the covers. Sweeper cover gets across to his left, slides and stops the ball, keeping the batsmen to a couple. 11 from this over as well, 43 in the last 4.
Another slower delivery, short in length, the skipper pulls it towards fine leg for a run.
WIDE. Another slower ball, this is down the leg side. Azam misses his tuck.
Slower delivery, outside off, Rizwan steers it behind point for a single.
Has hit one onto his calf there. Around off, Azam looks to punch but gets a thick inside edge onto his calf or ankle. Winces in pain. A run taken.
FOUR! WHACK! Just a fraction bit short, around off, but Babar Azam is quickly onto the pull. Backs away and lashes it through mid-wicket.
Full, down the leg side, Mohammad Rizwan falls over and flicks it towards fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Bad last ball spoils the over! Short, outside off, Babar camps back and punches it through the covers. Long off rushes to his left but cannot get there! 11 from the over, 32 in the last 3.
Down the leg side, Rizwan gets across, looks to sweep, misses the ball but at the last moment, manages to get some bat on it. The ball rolls off the under edge through fine leg. A single taken.
Short, outside off, Babar Azam cuts it to sweeper cover for a run.
Full, outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Around off, whipped through mid-wicket for a brace again.
Full, around off, Mohammad Rizwan works it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Gamble. Massive one. Matt Parkinson is back on. 7-0-46-1 so far.
A short ball, down the leg side, Babar looks to tuck but misses. The ball goes off his pads through fine leg and a couple of leg byes are taken. 10 from the over, 21 in the last 2.
A length ball, outside off, cutting back in sharply, Rizwan looks to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. He is in pain but manages to take a leg bye.

FOUR! A bit streaky but he will take it to get to his HALF CENTURY. In 42 balls. A length ball, around middle, Mohammad Rizwan gets across, looks to paddle but the ball takes the top edge and flies very fine, to the fine leg fence. The stand moves to 121 from 89 balls.
A short ball, outside off, into the body, coming in with the angle, Babar Azam comes down the track and pulls it towards backward square leg for one.
Around off, angling in, Mohammad Rizwan works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Outside off, dabbed towards third man for a single.
POWERPLAY 3 time. 5 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle now. Can Pakistan get 100 in the last 10?
Outside off, on a length, coming in, Azam backs away and from the middle-and-off line, pushes the ball to third man for one. 11 from the over, Saqib Mahmood's figures read 8-2-40-1 so far.

FOUR! There he goes again. Short, outside off, Babar Azam pulls it over wide mid on. This is the final over before the fielding restrictions get lifted. Remember, from the 41st over, you can have 5 fielders outside the 30-yard circle. Babar moves to 112 from 112 balls. The stand is worth 113 in 84 deliveries.
Around off, coming in, MR tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
A rare swing and a miss. Outside off, on a length, Rizwan walks into the shot and looks to thrash it through the off side but misses.
FOUR! WALLOP! Short, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan gets on top of the bounce, leaps and pulls it through mid-wicket. The ball races away.
A short ball, outside off, Babar Azam pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, Azam works it towards point and takes a quick single, beating the shy from the fielder towards the non-striker's end. The throw misses the stumps.
Outside off, worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Similar ball, similar shot, Azam does a repeat of the previous shot but gets a single this time.
Outside off, on a length, Babar Azam waits for the ball to arrive and then plays this extremely late through the vacant slip cordon towards third man. Two runs taken. 100-RUN STAND UP IN 76 BALLS!
Around off, Rizwan works it through mid-wicket for a single. Moves to 40 from 36 balls.

A slight halt in play. While completing the second run on the previous ball, he dived and while doing so, his hhead jerked a touch and the helmet hit the ground. That can hurt. The physio has been called for.
Short, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan cuts it through point for a couple.
Craig Overton returns. 6-0-26-0 so far.
Around off, pushed towards cover for a run.
A short ball, around middle, Azam pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Length ball, outside off, Babar flays hard without moving his feet and misses.
Around off, worked through square leg for a run.
Outside off, steered towards third man for a single.

FOUR! If only you could hear the roar! The crowd has gone bonkers. Babar Azam reaches his 14th ODI century in 104 balls. To imagine that it took him 15 balls to get his first run, it is commendable to see him cover up for the time taken early on and the composure shown. A real captain's knock, able to absorb the pressure and transfer it onto the opposition. Gets there by crunching it through point. He leaps in the air and punches his fists, showing how much this means to him. He has been under pressure for a while and this will delight his fans.

Outside off, short in length, Azam taps it behind point for a run.10 from the over, 200 UP FOR PAKISTAN. This last 50 has taken 39 balls, the fastest for Pakistan today. Brydon Carse's figures read 7-0-34-0 so far.

FOUR! Excellent batting. Carse drops it short again, outside off, Babar Azam latches onto the pull and hits it through mid-wicket, finding the gap with ease. A hit away from the century as he moves to 96.
Dropped short, outside off, Babar mistimes his pull to mid on.
Outside off, Rizwan guides it towards third man for a single.
FOUR! Sweet timing again! A short ball, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan pulls it through mid-wicket and the ball races away! The stand moves to 81 from 63 balls.
Outside off, on a length, Mohammad Rizwan pushes it towards cover.
Around off, angling in, Rizwan helps it through square leg for one more. Moves to 30 from 29 balls.
Short again, the cut shot again, Overton again. This time, it is straight to him and the batsmen get a single.
Another couple. Babar moves to 91 from 99 balls. A short ball, around middle, Azam helps it through square leg.

Great shot, good fielding. Good cricket all around. Fractionally short, outside off, Babar cuts it behind point. The timing is sweet and the ball races away towards the point fence. But Craig Overton races across to his left from sweeper cover, dives to his left and in one go, quickly gets up and releases the ball towards the keeper. Excellent. Two runs taken.
A short ball, outside off, Babar Azam mistimes his pull towards mid on.
On a length, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan guides it towards third man for a single.
Saqib Mahmood returns. 5-2-14-1 so far.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Short, around off, Rizwan pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Around off, on a length, Babar defends it close to his body. Looks to tap and run to the off side but the bowler quickly gets to the ball. However, they still make it through for the single.
ALMOST! Yorker, outside off, Babar, backing away to the leg side, attempts to push it through the off side but misses. Seemed like a woody sound was heard but the ball just missed the off stump!
Short, outside off, a touch wide, Mohammad Rizwan throws his bat at it and mistimes it through the covers for a run.
Around off, Babar Azam helps it through square leg for a single.
Brydon Carse comes on now. 5-0-20-0 so far.
The googly to end the over, around off, MR defends. 10 from the over, 20 in the last 2.
Around off, pushed down to long on for a run.

SIX! Fantastic hit! Tossed up, outside off, Babar comes down the track and launches this over mid off, who is three quarters of the way towards the ropes. Does not matter. Sails well over the ropes! Moves to 84 from 91 balls and the stand is worth 65 from 47 deliveries.
Around off, worked through mid on for one.
Outside off, fuller in length, spinning away, Babar Azam looks to drive but the ball takes the outside edge and dies through the slip region. A run taken.
Fuller, around middle, Mohammad Rizwan defends it to the leg side. A single taken.

DRINKS BREAK. Wow. Pakistan are finally back. Babar Azam amongst the runs means that the batting usually looks comfortable. He is looking well set to get to his 14th ODI century. 17 overs left. The stage is left. Is 300 coming? England have not quite been able to get the breakthroughs consistently today and hence, the bowlers have gone for runs. Can they bounce back in the death stages?
Around off, MR pushes it towards mid on for a quick single. Good running. 10 from the over, Lewis Gregory has been at the receiving end today - 7-0-42-0 so far.
Fuller, around off, watchfully defended.

FOUR! The body language is changing now, for Pakistan. They seem a lot more confident. Full, around middle, Rizwan punches this uppishly, right at his partner. Babar ducks and the ball races to the left of mid on, to the fence behind. Rizwan moves to 23 from 20 balls.
Outside off, pushed through point for a single.
FOUR! VIOLENCE! Short ball, around off, Babar pulls it through mid-wicket and the ball races away. 50-STAND IS UP IN 39 BALLS!
Outside off, on a length, Babar Azam drives it straight to mid off.
Fuller, outside off, driven wide of mid off for a run.
Around the middle stump, pushed towards long on for a single.

DROPPED! That was a toughie. Fuller, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan lunges to defend but the ball takes the inside edge and goes towards the keeper. Now, John Simpson is moving to his right and he has to change direction to his left, as the ball has hit the inside edge. Cannot hang on.
Around middle, short in length, Babar punches it down to long on for one.
The googly, around off, Mohammad Rizwan backs away and punches it through the covers for a run.
Mid on goes back now.
Short, outside off, Babar Azam cuts it behind point for a single.
Another short ball, Babar pulls it through mid-wicket for one more.
A short ball, outside off, pulled to deep mid-wicket for one more.
A short ball, delivered from the back of the hand, Rizwan looks to pull but the ball hits his gloves and goes down the leg side.
A short ball, around off, Azam pulls it through mid-wicket. The fielder gets to the ball and then dives near the ropes to pull the ball back in. Three runs taken.
Around off, dabbed to third man for a run.
A short ball, outside off, Babar hacks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, short in length, punched towards cover for a single.
Around off, watchfully defended to the leg side.
Down the leg side, the googly, nudged through fine leg for a single.
Outside off, pushed through point for a single.
Down the leg side, Babar looks to sweep but the ball hits his right glove, then the wrist and then drops down to the leg side.
FOUR! Fine shot. Looped up, outside off, Babar Azam comes down the track and lofts it over mid off. He is just starting to find his groove.
Outside off, steered through third man for a single.
SIX! Powerful hit! A short ball, outside off, Babar launches into it and pulls it massively over mid-wicket!
Outside off, bunted through the covers for a run.
Outside off, this is steered towards third man for a single.
Short, outside off, pushed towards cover.
Full, around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Lewis Gregory is into the attack. 4-0-15-0 so far.
A full ball, outside off, Rizwan looks to paddle but gets a top edge over the keeper, through fine leg. A couple taken.
Outside off, pushed towards mid on.
Outside off, Babar pushes it towards long on for a single, 50 FOR THE SKIPPER.
Around off, nudged to the leg side for a run.
WIDE. Down the leg side, Rizwan looks to sweep but misses again.
FOUR! Full again, this time Rizwan connects with his sweep and gets it powerfully through mid-wicket.
Full, down the leg side, Rizwan looks to sweep but misses. The ball hits his pads and lobs in the air, wide of the keeper.
Outside off, driven through point where Philip Salt does well.
Outside off, chopped down in front of point for a single.
WIDE.  Short and down the leg side, Rizwan misses out on the pull.
FOUR! A short ball, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
A short ball, pulled to deep square leg for a run.
Outside off, pushed through cover for a single.
Full, around middle, this is driven through mid on. The fielder quickly gets across to his left and makes a good stop.
Fuller, outside off, Mohammad Rizwan defends solidly. 2 runs and a wicket in the over, Matt Parkinson's figures read 3-0-15-1.
Mohammad Rizwan walks in at number 4, replacing Imam-ul-Haq.

OUT! BOWLED! Boy o boy, that's a ripper from Matt 'Warne' Parkinson! Tell you what, Shadab Khan will be loving this in the dressing room. It is England who are going to bat second. Beautifully tossed up, wide outside off, Imam-ul-Haq reaches out to drive. But the ball pitches, spins in a mile, goes past the inside edge and hits the stumps! Just a little bit of rough outside the left-hander's off stump and that was enough for the ball to spin. The 92-run stand is broken and Imam walks back after a fabulous innings.
Around middle, the googly, IUH comes down the track and hits it straight back to the bowler. Parkinson misfields but short mid-wicket quickly mops up.
Fuller, outside off, Babar Azam pushes it through the covers for a run.
A touch short, around middle, Imam nudges it through square leg for a single.
Full, around middle, Imam-ul-Haq comes down the track and defends.
Outside off, steered towards third man. Surprisingly, Imam wants the second but this time, Babar denies. The stand moves to 90 from 122 balls.
A quick bouncer, around middle, Imam thinks about the pull but then bails out. Stokes has two men in the deep on the leg side for the pull or hook.

EDGED, FOUR! No slip and Imam profits. Short and wide outside off, Imam-ul-Haq throws his bat at it as he looks to cut. But he is too close to the ball and gets a thick outside edge. It flies towards first slip but that area is vacant. The ball then races down to the third man fence.
A short ball, around off, Babar pulls it through mid-wicket for one.

On a good length, outside off, Imam-ul-Haq steers it through third man for a run. 50 UP FOR IMAM-UL-HAQ. In just 66 balls. He should have been out lbw in the very first over, which the umpire did not give and Stokes did not review, but since then, he has been excellent.
Around middle, Babar Azam nudges it through mid-wicket for a single.
Floated, around middle and off, Azam pushes it past the bowler, towards long off for one. 10 from the over.

The googly, outside off, Imam-ul-Haq goes back and cuts it to the right of Saqib Mahmood at short third man. Deep point gets to the ball and the batters take three runs. 100 UP FOR PAKISTAN. 157 balls left.
Slower through the air, around off, Babar is down the track this time, pushing the ball down to long on for a run.

FOUR! Up and over. That was thrashed. Full, outside off, Babar Azam gets underneath it and blasts it over Ben Stokes at mid off. Just for a brief moment, Stokes thought he could get across to his right but the ball went well over him.
Tossed up, around off, Babar Azam comes down the track now and flicks, but finds short mid-wicket.
Fuller, around middle, Imam-ul-Haq comes down the track and pushes it towards long on for a single.

On a good length, outside off, the skipper punches it behind point for a couple. We should have been done with the over but the umpire is not done yet. He is actually talking to Stokes and probably telling him that he is too close to overstepping. Just a friendly warning, one supposes. No no ball signalled.
Around off, on a length, left alone.
Fuller, around off, angling in, Azam works it towards square leg.
On a good length, around off, Babar works it towards short mid-wicket.
Fractionally short, outside off, Babar Azam cuts it behind point for a couple. The stand moves to 70 from 106 balls.
Fuller, around middle and leg, Imam-ul-Haq flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

Around middle, Imam tucks it through mid-wicket for one. Three singles from Parkinson's first over. It will be interesting to see how he goes today. In the previous two games, he has come on at a time when Pakistan were struggling, having lost 3-4 wickets. Today, he has come on in the middle of a good partnership.
Fuller, around off, BA drives it towards long off for a single.
Looped up, outside off, Azam lunges and defends towards cover.
Uses his feet, does Babar, gets to the pitch of the ball and flicks it towards short mid-wicket.
Around middle and leg, Babar Azam works it straight to square leg.
Full, around off, Imam-ul-Haq is straightaway down the track to push the ball down to long on for a single.
We are going to see spin for the first time. Matt Parkinson, the wrist spinner from Lancashire, is onto bowl.

Ahhh... another piece of miscommunication. Around off, angling away, Imam punched it behind point and set off for a single. Now, third man had to cover some area to his left and there was a big opportunity for the second. Accordingly, Babar turned blind for the second. But for some reason, Imam is happy with the single and sends his skipper back. Poor running.
Outside off, this is driven on the up through the covers for a run.
Fuller, outside off, Babar drives it straight to short extra cover.
FOUR! TONK! That was hit really hard. Stokes bangs it in and Babar immediately hangs back. Pulls it with authority through mid-wicket. Moves to 32 from 50 balls, in a stand of 62 from 96.
Around off, on a length, Babar Azam flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Starts off with a straightish ball, Imam-ul-Haq tickles it towards fine leg for a single.
A loud cheer goes around the ground as Ben Stokes takes matters into his own hands.
Down the leg side, Imam tucks it towards fine leg for one more.
Around middle, short in length, the skipper nudges it wide of mid-wicket for a single.
On a good length, outside off, angling away, Imam-ul-Haq steers it towards third man for a run.

NOT OUT. Safe as a house. But there are communication issues with these two. Around off, Imam punched it towards cover and called for a single. Babar responded but then, got sent back. The fielder at cover-point stopped the ball, took an aim and fired his missile. Hit the stumps at the bowler's end and got the crowd excited, but when referred upstairs, one replay was enough to indicate that Babar was back in.
Run out? There is a direct hit and it is referred upstairs. Babar looks in though. Yes, the replay confirms.
Blue skies, finally! The sun is out in full bloom now.

Interesting approach from both sides. Pakistan have understandably not panicked and stuck to what they feel is their best XI. England, on the other hand, have resisted the temptation of fielding bench players considering that the series is done and are going with what they believe is their strongest team to inflict a whitewash. Let's hope for a cracker then.
Pakistan (UNCHANGED XI) - Imam-ul-Haq, Fakhar Zaman, Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Saud Shakeel, Sohaib Maqsood, Shadab Khan, Faheem Ashraf, Hasan Ali, Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf.
England (UNCHANGED XI) - Philip Salt, Dawid Malan, Zak Crawley, James Vince, Ben Stokes (C), John Simpson (WK), Lewis Gregory, Craig Overton, Brydon Carse, Saqib Mahmood and Matt Parkinson.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. It has landed in Ben Stokes' favour and ENGLAND WILL CHASE.

WEATHER REPORT - The most frequently talked about topic in England, Ireland and Sri Lanka. NO RAIN CLOUDS in the sky. Conditions pleasant for cricket and we should have an uninterrupted game of cricket. Hurrah!

What's wrong with Pakistan? One would say, lack of match practice. In the pre-Covid era, teams used to tour other countries, play a couple of wam-up matches, get used to the conditions and then begin an international series. Sadly, in this Covid era, practice matches have been abolished and teams can only play an intra-squad game, which is not actually that useful, as a county opposition can be. So, looking on the brighter side, Pakistan have had their two warm-up games done and tonight might see their first decent performance in the tour. Remember, there are 3 T20Is to follow after this. So there is plenty of cricket left.

India have one team playing in England while another is in Sri Lanka. Yet, both teams are equally capable of winning either series. In fact, if social media memes and jokes are to be believed, especially, former England skipper, Michael Vaughan, any team from the Indian T20 League can be as dominant as the senior one! Regarding England, this is not their first-choice team. It is not their B-team either. It is their C-team, which has been made overnight, due to a Covid spread in the original squad. But in both matches, do you actually feel that this is a county side? England and India's futures look very, very bright.

Why Dhoni and Morgan, do you ask? If you remember, before the 2015 ODI World Cup, there was a tri-series in Australia, which involved the hosts of course, along with England and India. Australia were way too dominant in that series and not surprisingly, pulvarised everyone in the mega tournament to follow. England were able to beat only Scotland and Afghanistan during the World Cup, while India fared way better, reaching the semi finals. However, it was after that, that the teams started to focus on their future. Look at India and England then - look at them now.

Two matches done, series done. Pakistan were shocked in the opener, England showed that it was no fluke in the second. As MS Dhoni and Eoin Morgan revel seeing the future stocks of their respective countries, can other teams start taking notice? 'Youngsters need to win us games' is the motto of Misbah-ul-Haq. Can Pakistan restore that faith in him? Hello and a warm welcome to the third and final ODI between England and Pakistan in Birmingham.
